questions.text: In the headline cell (dissolved zinc, Cement Creek, Colorado River Watch), what is the flow-adjusted level change at the 2015-08-05 release in the primary specification, with its Newey-West 95% interval, and which of the three pre-registered conclusions applies?
questions.notes: Primary specification: interval includes zero; rule 3 applies. The 2010 and 2013 pre-period starts exclude zero (grid.pre2010.*, grid.pre2013.*); the exploratory cleaned refit (explore.clean.*) excludes zero.

questions.text: How does the headline level change vary across the 27-fit sensitivity grid (pre-period start 2005/2010/2013, plume-window end, post-period end), and does the sign or significance depend on the pre-period start?
questions.notes: Point estimates near -20 percent for every pre-period start with the 2025 post-period end; the interval excludes zero only for the 2010 and 2013 starts. The post-period end matters more: ending in 2016 the change is positive.

questions.text: Where do the blind change-points (PELT and binary segmentation on the monthly flow-adjusted residuals of the headline cell) fall relative to the release (2015-08) and the treatment-plant start (2015-10)?
questions.notes: Pre-registered search: strongest split 65 months before the release (artefact-driven). Cleaned series (exploratory): strongest split 2016-02, six months after the release and four after the plant start.

questions.text: Does the upstream control (Animas above Cement Creek) show a change of the same sign, and what is the difference-in-differences level change for Cement Creek and for the Animas below Silverton?
questions.notes: The control's pre-registered -21 percent is driven by three coded zeros; cleaned it is -11 percent with an interval including zero. DiD level change -24 percent with a differential downward slope.

questions.text: Across the 64 reach x constituent x fraction cells at the primary specification, how many are estimable, how many have raw p < 0.05, and how many survive Benjamini-Hochberg at 5% FDR?
questions.notes: 52 of 64 estimable; 7 raw p below 0.05; 0 survive Benjamini-Hochberg at 5 percent FDR. Cleaned (exploratory): 9 and 0.

questions.text: How did sampling intensity, organisations and reporting limits change across the release date, and which series are comparable across it?
questions.notes: Sampling events rose about 2.5-fold and organisations from four to nine after the release; only Colorado River Watch is comparable across it (one method, monthly, 2005-2025). Reporting limits were unrecorded before 2013 and rose for several metals after 2019; arsenic is not estimable anywhere.
